blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation
s: Atrial fibrillation (sometimes called afib or AF) is a type of heart rhythm problem where your heartbeat is not steady.
See a GP if you think you may have it.

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Symptoms of atrial fibrillation
s: The main symptoms of atrial fibrillation are:

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Symptoms of atrial fibrillation
s: an irregular heartbeat, where your pulse is not steady

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Symptoms of atrial fibrillation
s: suddenly feeling like your heart is pounding, racing, fluttering, skipping or missing a beat (heart palpitations) – this may last for a few seconds up to a few minutes

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Symptoms of atrial fibrillation
s: a heartbeat faster than 100 beats per minute

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Symptoms of atrial fibrillation
s: feeling very tired

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Symptoms of atrial fibrillation
s: finding it harder to exercise

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Symptoms of atrial fibrillation
s: chest pain or tightness

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Symptoms of atrial fibrillation
s: feeling short of breath, lightheaded, dizzy or like you might faint

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Symptoms of atrial fibrillation
s: Sometimes there are no symptoms, and atrial fibrillation is found as part of a routine check-up or when you're having tests for something else.

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Symptoms of atrial fibrillation
s: If you do get symptoms, they may start and stop on their own (paroxysmal atrial fibrillation) or stop after treatment (persistent atrial fibrillation).

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Symptoms of atrial fibrillation
s: Over time, you may always have symptoms (permanent atrial fibrillation).

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you think you may have symptoms of atrial fibrillation

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you have heart palpitations that keep happening or are getting worse

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you have been diagnosed with atrial fibrillation and treatment is not helping your symptoms

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: You currently have a fast or irregular heartbeat, and any of these symptoms:

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: chest pain

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: shortness of breath

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: sweating

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: feeling or being sick

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: fainting, feeling dizzy or falling over

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: a severe headache

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: weakness or numbness on one side of your face or body

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: blurred vision or loss of sight

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: confusion or difficulty speaking

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: Do not drive yourself to A&E.

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: The person you speak to at 999 will give you advice about what to do.

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Tests for atrial fibrillation
s: If a GP thinks you could have atrial fibrillation, they will refer you to a heart specialist (cardiologist).

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Tests for atrial fibrillation
s: At your appointment, they will ask about your symptoms and check your heart rate.

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Tests for atrial fibrillation
s: You will also have tests to see if anything else could be causing your symptoms and to check your heart rhythm.
Tests may include:

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Tests for atrial fibrillation
s: an electrocardiogram (ECG)

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Tests for atrial fibrillation
s: an echocardiogram (echo)

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Tests for atrial fibrillation
s: a chest X-ray

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Tests for atrial fibrillation
s: blood tests

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Treatment for atrial fibrillation
s: If you have been diagnosed with atrial fibrillation, you will have regular check-ups to make sure your symptoms are under control.

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Treatment for atrial fibrillation
s: You may be given medicine to:

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Treatment for atrial fibrillation
s: control the rate and rhythm of your heart, such as beta blockers

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Treatment for atrial fibrillation
s: lower the risk of blood clots or stroke (anticoagulants)

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Treatment for atrial fibrillation
s: Other possible treatments for atrial fibrillation include:

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Treatment for atrial fibrillation
s: burning, freezing or using high-energy electrical pulses to destroy a section of your heart (ablation)

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Treatment for atrial fibrillation
s: using electricity to reset your heart rhythm (electrical cardioversion)

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Treatment for atrial fibrillation
s: having a pacemaker or implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) fitted

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Treatment for atrial fibrillation
s: Sometimes atrial fibrillation can be caused by another health condition or medicine.
In these cases, treating the condition or stopping the medicine can improve the symptoms.

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Things you can do yourself to help with atrial fibrillation
s: In addition to treatment you might need, there are things you can do yourself to help with symptoms of atrial fibrillation and lower the chances of complications.

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Things you can do yourself to help with atrial fibrillation > Do avoid triggers such as caffeine, spicy food, stress, dehydration and lack of sleep try to keep to a healthy weight eat a balanced diet exercise regularly – aim to do at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise a week, like walking, bike riding or gardening Don't
s: do not smoke

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Things you can do yourself to help with atrial fibrillation > Do avoid triggers such as caffeine, spicy food, stress, dehydration and lack of sleep try to keep to a healthy weight eat a balanced diet exercise regularly – aim to do at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise a week, like walking, bike riding or gardening Don't
s: do not drink too much alcohol

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Things you can do yourself to help with atrial fibrillation > Do avoid triggers such as caffeine, spicy food, stress, dehydration and lack of sleep try to keep to a healthy weight eat a balanced diet exercise regularly – aim to do at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise a week, like walking, bike riding or gardening Don't
s: do not exercise too much or too hard – this can trigger atrial fibrillation

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: Atrial fibrillation is caused by a problem with the electrical system that makes your heart beat.

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: Anyone can get it, but you may be more likely to get it if:

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: you're aged 55 or older

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: you're a man

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: you're living with obesity or overweight

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: you smoke

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: you take certain medicines, such as levothyroxine, lithium or some asthma medicines like salbutamol

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: you do endurance sports like long-distance running, cycling or skiing

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: Atrial fibrillation can also be caused by another condition such as:

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: high blood pressure

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: heart conditions like heart failure, mitral valve problems or Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: a heart attack

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: chronic kidney disease

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism)

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: diabetes

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Causes of atrial fibrillation
s: sleep apnoea

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > How atrial fibrillation affects your life
s: There is currently no cure for atrial fibrillation, but treatment should help manage the symptoms and lower the risk of complications like blood clots, stroke and heart failure.

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > How atrial fibrillation affects your life
s: You should be able to carry on doing most things as usual, including exercise.
But avoid intense exercise and try not to exercise when you're having symptoms of atrial fibrillation.
Check with your doctor if you're not sure what exercise you can do.

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > How atrial fibrillation affects your life
s: If you drive you may need to tell the DVLA that you have atrial fibrillation.
Your doctor will be able to tell you if this applies to you.

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > How atrial fibrillation affects your life
s: There might also be other practical things you need to think about if you have a heart condition, like travelling abroad with medicine, and changes to health or travel insurance.

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Help and support for atrial fibrillation
s: While atrial fibrillation can usually be managed, living with a heart condition can be worrying.

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Help and support for atrial fibrillation
s: You may find it helpful to get support from other people with atrial fibrillation, either at a local support group or online.

blocks.path: Atrial fibrillation > Help and support for atrial fibrillation
s: There are also national charities that can offer information, help and support.
